data.result:
I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. This involves creating a bare git repository, a post-receive hook to deploy files, and a web server on port 8080.

Here's what you need to do on your server computer:

## 1. Create the bare git repository

```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare
```

## 2. Create the deployment directory

```bash
mkdir -p /var/www/html
```

## 3. Set up the post-receive hook

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
git --work-tree=/var/www/html --git-dir=/git/server checkout -f
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

This hook runs after every push and checks out the latest commit to `/var/www/html`.

## 4. Start a web server on port 8080

Choose one option:

**Option A: Using Python (simple, no dependencies)**
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

**Option B: Using Node.js (if available)**
```bash
cd /var/www/html
npx http-server -p 8080
```

**Option C: Using nginx (production-grade)**

Create `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default` or a new config:
```nginx
server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
}
```

Then start nginx:
```bash
sudo systemctl start nginx
```

## Now test it

From your client computer:

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-repo
cd my-repo
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

Should output: `hello world`

The post-receive hook automatically deploys your files to `/var/www/html` on every push, and the web server serves them on port 8080.

I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. This involves creating a bare git repository, a post-receive hook to deploy files, and a web server on port 8080.

Here's what you need to do on your server computer:

## 1. Create the bare git repository

```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare
```

## 2. Create the deployment directory

```bash
mkdir -p /var/www/html
```

## 3. Set up the post-receive hook

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
git --work-tree=/var/www/html --git-dir=/git/server checkout -f
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

This hook runs after every push and checks out the latest commit to `/var/www/html`.

## 4. Start a web server on port 8080

Choose one option:

**Option A: Using Python (simple, no dependencies)**
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

**Option B: Using Node.js (if available)**
```bash
cd /var/www/html
npx http-server -p 8080
```

**Option C: Using nginx (production-grade)**

Create `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default` or a new config:
```nginx
server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
}
```

Then start nginx:
```bash
sudo systemctl start nginx
```

## Now test it

From your client computer:

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-repo
cd my-repo
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

Should output: `hello world`

The post-receive hook automatically deploys your files to `/var/www/html` on every push, and the web server serves them on port 8080.
